title: Exceptional coefficient-system mate with unit and composition equations
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E\subset S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sf-setting]. For $T=X,Y$, put $A_{n,T}=(R/\ell^n)_T$, $B_{n,T}=(S/\ell^n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site, and use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Write $\mathcal N_A(T),\mathcal N_B(T)$ for their normalized constructible subcategories with uniform cohomological and Tor bounds [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and $C_T=-\otimes^L_{A_{\bullet,T}}B_{\bullet,T}$ for scalar extension of whole systems [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Twists mean [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $P_A=Rf_{!,A,\bullet}\dashv G_A=f^!_{A,\bullet}$ and $P_B\dashv G_B$ for the specified tower adjunctions, with units $\eta_A,\eta_B$ and counits $\epsilon_A,\epsilon_B$ [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Fix the same compactification for the two compact-support functors [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Let $b:C_YP_A\xrightarrow{\sim}P_BC_X$ be the coefficient comparison formed by the proper direct-image coefficient mate followed by the open-extension tensor identification, as in [lem-sp-field-shriek-system-comparison]. For $K\in\mathcal N_A(Y)$ define $c_K$ as the $P_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $C_Y\epsilon_{A,K}\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1}$. These are natural isomorphisms of whole coefficient systems $c:C_XG_A\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BC_Y$. Evaluation gives exactly the finite exceptional comparison $c_{R/\ell^n,S/\ell^n}(K_n)$ of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Its quotient transitions agree with the two mixed paths from $R/\ell^n$ to $S/\ell^m$ and with the specified quotient mates of $G_A,G_B$ in [det-sp-tower-gluing](3). In the tower derived categories themselves,
$$\epsilon_{B,C_YK}\circ P_B(c_K)=C_Y(\epsilon_{A,K})\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1},$$
$$G_B(b_M)\circ c_{P_AM}\circ C_X(\eta_{A,M})=\eta_{B,C_XM}.$$
For successive finite extensions $E\subset F\subset L$, the composite of the two $c$ transformations is the $c$ for $E\subset L$, using the canonical tensor associators; identity extensions give identities. These equations do not rely on faithfulness of general derived evaluation.

proof.text: Apply lem-sp-field-shriek-system-comparison to obtain simultaneous Models D and proper/open Laws b. Apply lem-sp-field-exceptional-normalized-adjoints for Domains a, Adjoints A and the right-adjoint quotient formula.

component is the actual adjunction transpose. Applying the inverse Hom equivalence gives its counit law. Apply homEquiv_naturality_left_square to naturality of the inverse support comparison and of the scalar-extended counit, giving naturality. For the unit equation transpose both words, use naturality of the support comparison and the target counit, then the defining component counit equation and the source triangle identity; cancellation of the invertible support comparison proves the unit law.

Apply lem-sp-field-exceptional-finite-compatibility for the evaluation and mixed laws and finite invertibility. Conjugate the evaluated component by sourceEvaluation and targetEvaluation to obtain its invertibility at each finite level. The detects field of D.base.calculus, supplied by det-sp-tower-shriek-levels, gives ambient invertibility. The fully faithful inclusion of the normalized full subcategory reflects it.

For transitions, systemReduction is the transpose of the natural derivedTransition followed by the section-identity restriction comparison. Its naturality square follows by homEquiv_naturality_right_square applied to that natural transformation, at the actual component. This proves the transition law without equality detection by evaluation.

Prove the coefficient composition law by transposing both words under the last adjunction. Naturality of the last counit and the second support comparison, followed by the two defining counit equations, reduces the successive word to the scalar associator applied to the first counit. The composition clause of b identifies the remaining support word. Cancel its invertible components; injectivity gives composition. For identity, transpose component followed by the exceptional image of the scalar unitor. Naturality of the counit and scalar unitor reduces to b.identity, then inverse cancellation. Bundle these proved laws with the finite and quotient laws into Laws.

proof_origin.place: (2), counit transpose, finite comparisons and quotient compatibility
